title: Ord Interface
concept: The Ord interface defines total ordering — `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` — enabling sorting, binary search, and priority-based data structures.
why: Without Ord, you can't sort collections or use ordered data structures like BTreeMap. Ord is the gateway to algorithms that depend on ordering.
tips: Implement Ord to enable .sort(), .binary_search(), and ordered collections
Use the @pre-existing cmp on primitive fields — self.age.cmp(&other.age)
For multi-field comparison, chain with match: try first field, fall through to second
Consistency rule: a.cmp(&b) == Ordering::Equal must imply a == b (Eq consistency)
common_mistakes: Implementing Ord with inconsistent PartialEq — a == b but a.cmp(&b) != Equal
Using > or < in the Ord implementation — that would be recursive (use cmp on fields)
Forgetting that Ord requires Eq — implement both
